parameters.query:
SELECT article_id, title, source, url,
       to_char(published_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS published_date,
       category, summary, relevance_score
FROM processed_articles
WHERE newsletter_week = $1::date
  AND status = 'selected'
ORDER BY relevance_score DESC, published_date DESC NULLS LAST;

parameters.text:
==Here are this week's selected articles:

{{ $json.articles.map(a => `[${a.article_id}] (${a.category}) ${a.title} — ${a.summary}`).join('\n') }}

Produce, all in English:
- "subject_hook": a short hook of max 60 characters mentioning 2-3 key topics of the week. No emoji.
- "introduction": 2 sentences presenting the week's main themes.
- "trending": { "title": max 6 words, "text": 2 sentences } — the dominant trend across the articles.
- "insights": exactly 3 short punchy editorial lines (max 90 characters each), like quotes.
- "short_titles": for EVERY article, { "article_id": exact id from brackets, "short_title": headline of max 6 words }.
- "image_keywords": 4-5 keywords summarizing the week.
- "image_prompt": one sentence describing a concrete visual metaphor for the TRENDING topic (objects, scene, composition). No text, no letters, no logos, no brand names, no real people.

messageValues.message: You are the editor-in-chief of 'AI Foundry Weekly', the internal AI newsletter of NTT DATA's AI Foundry team. You write short, sharp, factual editorial copy in English. Never invent facts that are not in the provided articles.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO newsletters (newsletter_id, week, introduction)
VALUES ($1, $2::date, $3)
ON CONFLICT (newsletter_id) DO UPDATE SET introduction = EXCLUDED.introduction
RETURNING newsletter_id, sent_at;

-- People who already received THIS newsletter (safe re-runs, no double send)
SELECT DISTINCT subscriber_email
FROM delivery_log
WHERE newsletter_id = $1
  AND status = 'sent';

parameters.query:
WITH n AS (
  UPDATE newsletters SET sent_at = NOW()
  WHERE newsletter_id = $1
  RETURNING newsletter_id
),
a AS (
  UPDATE processed_articles SET status = 'sent'
  WHERE newsletter_week = $2::date AND status = 'selected'
  RETURNING article_id
)
SELECT $1 AS newsletter_id,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM n) AS newsletter_marked_sent,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM a) AS articles_marked_sent;
